a: Use your left pinky finger. A is its home key, so let your pinky rest on A whenever you are not using it.
Keep your left pinky finger curved and resting lightly on A. Try typing 'a sad lad' slowly without looking down.
b: Use your left pointer finger. Reach down and to the right from F, then go straight back to F.
B is a long stretch for your left pointer finger, so move your whole hand a little from F instead of twisting it. Never use your right hand for B.
c: Use your left middle finger. Reach down from D to C, then bring it back to D.
Keep your left middle finger on D and curl it down to C. Practise 'cat', 'cod' and 'ice' slowly and smoothly.
d: Use your left middle finger. D is its home key, so keep that finger resting on D.
Your left middle finger should press D without looking. Practise 'dad did add' while your other fingers stay on A, S and F.
e: Use your left middle finger. Reach up from D to E, then bring it straight back to D.
E is the most common letter in English, so it is worth getting right. Try 'see', 'tree' and 'free' with your left middle finger going up from D and back.
f: Use your left pointer finger. F is its home key. Feel for the little bump on F to find it without looking.
Your left pointer finger lives on F. After every reach (to R, T, G, V or B) bring it home to F before the next letter.
g: Use your left pointer finger. Slide one key to the right from F, then come back to F.
Only your left pointer finger types G. Stretch it right from F without moving your other fingers off A, S and D.
h: Use your right pointer finger. Slide one key to the left from J, then come back to J.
Only your right pointer finger types H. Stretch it left from J while your other fingers stay on K, L and ;.
i: Use your right middle finger. Reach up from K to I, then bring it back to K.
Practise 'it is in' slowly. Your right middle finger reaches up from K to I, and your other fingers stay on the home row.
j: Use your right pointer finger. J is its home key. Feel for the little bump on J to find it without looking.
Your right pointer finger lives on J. After reaching for U, Y, H, N or M, always bring it home to J.
k: Use your right middle finger. K is its home key, so keep that finger resting on K.
Practise 'kick' and 'kite' slowly. Your right middle finger presses K without leaving the home row.
l: Use your right ring finger. L is its home key, so keep that finger resting on L.
Keep your right ring finger curved over L. Practise 'all', 'fall' and 'hill' to get used to pressing L twice.
m: Use your right pointer finger. Reach down from J to M, then bring it back to J.
Curl your right pointer finger down from J to press M. Practise 'mum', 'jam' and 'mojo' slowly.
n: Use your right pointer finger. Reach down and a little left from J to N, then go back to J.
N sits just below and left of J. Your right pointer finger reaches it; don't use your left hand. Try 'nine' and 'nap'.
o: Use your right ring finger. Reach up from L to O, then bring it back to L.
Your right ring finger reaches up from L to O. Practise 'look', 'pool' and 'too', bringing the finger back to L each time.
p: Use your right pinky finger. Reach up from the ; key to P, then go back to ;.
P is a reach for your weakest finger. Keep your right pinky finger curved, reach up from ; to P, and practise 'pop' and 'pup' slowly.
q: Use your left pinky finger. Reach up from A to Q, then bring it back to A.
Q is rare but easy to miss. Your left pinky finger reaches up from A; keep your other fingers on S, D and F. Q is nearly always followed by U.
r: Use your left pointer finger. Reach up from F to R, then bring it back to F.
Practise 'rr' words like 'error' and 'mirror'. Your left pointer finger goes up from F to R and back each time.
s: Use your left ring finger. S is its home key, so keep that finger resting on S.
Your left ring finger lives on S. Practise 'sass' and 'miss' without letting your hand drift off A S D F.
t: Use your left pointer finger. Reach up and to the right from F to T, then go back to F.
T is very common. Your left pointer finger stretches up and right from F. Practise 'that', 'tent' and 'test'.
u: Use your right pointer finger. Reach up from J to U, then bring it back to J.
Your right pointer finger goes straight up from J to U. Practise 'up', 'run' and 'fun' slowly and smoothly.
v: Use your left pointer finger. Reach down from F to V, then bring it back to F.
Curl your left pointer finger down from F to press V. Practise 'van', 'have' and 'five'.
w: Use your left ring finger. Reach up from S to W, then bring it back to S.
Your left ring finger goes up from S to W. Practise 'we', 'was' and 'wow', keeping your pinky resting on A.
x: Use your left ring finger. Reach down from S to X, then bring it back to S.
X is a short reach down for your left ring finger from S. Practise 'box', 'six' and 'fox' slowly.
y: Use your right pointer finger. Reach up and to the left from J to Y, then go back to J.
Y is easy to mix up with T. Use your right pointer finger from J, not your left hand. Practise 'yes', 'you' and 'yay'.
z: Use your left pinky finger. Reach down from A to Z, then bring it back to A.
Z is a reach down for your left pinky finger from A. Keep your wrist still and practise 'zoo' and 'zip'.
space: Tap the space bar with your thumb while your other fingers stay on the home row (A S D F and J K L ;).
Use only one thumb for the space bar every time, and keep your fingers on the home row (A S D F and J K L ;) while you tap it.
great_job: Great job! None of your keys have a high mistake rate. Keep your fingers on the home row (A S D F and J K L ;) and try a harder level.
home_row: Start with your fingers on the home row (A S D F and J K L ;). Reach up or down from there for this key, then bring your finger straight back.
tip_of_the_day: Keep your fingers on the home row (A S D F and J K L ;) whenever you are not pressing a key.
Feel for the little bumps on F and J. They let you find the home row without looking down.
Look at the screen, not at your hands. It feels slow at first, but it makes you much faster.
Accuracy first, speed second. Typing slowly without mistakes is the fastest way to get faster.
Sit up straight with your feet flat on the floor and your wrists slightly raised off the desk.
Use the thumb you are most comfortable with for the space bar, and use the same one every time.
Ten minutes of practice every day is better than one hour once a week. Keep your streak going!
Each finger has its own keys. Bring every finger back to its home key after you press a key.
